newsitem.title: USA: Clinton bars troops from Bosnia manhunt.
newsitem.headline: Clinton bars troops from Bosnia manhunt.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Wednesday ruled out expanding the mission of a NATO-led peacekeeping force in Bosnia to track down and arrest warcrimes suspects.

"We can't expect people who are sent into a very volatile situation and asked to stabilise borders ... and do all the other things. You can't expect these same people to do that other work," Clinton said during a visit to the Defence Department.
Clinton was at the sprawling U.S. military headquarters for talks with new Defence Secretary William Cohen and top U.S. commanders from around the world, who are holding a two-day meeting here.
During a picture-taking session in a Pentagon conference room, he reiterated long-standing administration policy that peacekeeping troops should not be used for police functions in Bosnia.

"If they come in contact with people who are wanted and where there is, in effect, a warrant out for them, they ought to apprehend them. But I think it would be very difficult for them to do the (peacekeeping) mission, particularly with this smaller number of people and, in effect, spend full time doing that," Clinton said.

White House and Pentagon officials said this week the United States and NATO allies supported the idea of a police force to go after war criminals although no form for that force has been decided. Clinton said on Wednesday he believed any such unit should be attached to the international war crimes tribunal in The Hague and charged with policing war crimes wherever they occurred.
